newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen A shares dive at noon, hurt by bank.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares dive at noon, hurt by bank.

text.p: Shenzhen's domestic currency A share index fell sharply at midday on Wednesday, pushed down by heavy losses in the market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
The index slid 17.62 points or 3.92 percent to 431.81 on turnover of 3.5 billion yuan.
There was no trading in the city's hard currency B shares on Thursday due to a Hong Kong market holiday to mark the reversion of the territory to China at midnight on June 30.
"Sudden sharp falls in Development Bank triggered extensive selling in other shares," an analyst with Hainan Provincial Trust and Investment Co said in Shenzhen.
The bank lost 1.44 yuan to 36.30 yuan on volume of 6.88 million shares, making it the third most actively traded stock.

Brokers said the bank's plunge was caused in part by a front-page report in the China Securities newspaper on Wednesday that Shenzhen should re-compile its sub-index, in which the bank has a 33 percent weighting.
The sub-index, which only covers 40 listed firms, is no longer representative of the overall market after a sharp increase in the number of Shenzhen-listed companies, the newspaper said.
The number of the sub-index's components should be expanded and the bank's weighting should be reduced, it added.
The sub-index fell 194.64 points or 3.83 percent to 4886.80 at midday on Wednesday.
Brokers said some institutional investors have been seeking to influence the market trend by manipulating the bank's shares.
They also said the Hong Kong handover was not a factor in the morning's decline.
"The (Hong Kong) handover is now no longer a factor in the Shenzhen market because investors have already been preparing for the event for a long time," said a broker with China Guotai Securities.
Brokers said they expected the market to consolidate over the next few sessions, with investors awaiting new trading incentives.
Shenzhen-based Century Plaza Hotel was the biggest loser, plunging 0.85 yuan or 9.98 percent to 7.67 yuan.
